background: Career assistant hired by Phoenix in June 2025 as a first-time head coach after Mike Budenholzer's one-season flop. Rose from video coordinator roots: Michigan State (under Tom Izzo, where he overlapped with future Suns GM Brian Gregory), Atlanta Hawks video/player development (2013-16 under Budenholzer), Brooklyn Nets assistant (2016-22 under Kenny Atkinson, then Steve Nash), Los Angeles Lakers assistant (2022-24 under Darvin Ham) and Cleveland Cavaliers assistant on Atkinson's 64-18 staff (2024-25). Pitched at hiring as a detail-obsessed, development-minded 'culture reset' coach who would make the Suns play harder, faster and more connected after the Durant/Beal era. Was ranked 30th of 30 head coaches by Bleacher Report before the 2025-26 season, yet the post-Durant Suns were widely cited as one of the league's biggest overachievers in 2025-26 behind Devin Booker, a hard-playing wing group (Dillon Brooks, Ryan Dunn, Royce O'Neale, Grayson Allen) and a possession-battle identity built on offensive rebounding, forced turnovers and tempo. Exact 2025-26 record and postseason result were not verifiable in this session.

The only retrieved evidence is incidental: Bleacher Report's preseason 2025-26 ranking (No. 30), CBS's 2026 COY piece naming the Suns as overachievers, and a Eurohoops recap of Phoenix beating San Antonio. Background, scheme tags and most scores rest on the researcher's prior knowledge of Ott's hiring and the 2025-26 Suns' identity (possession battle, offensive rebounding, ball pressure, Booker-centric offense) and should be treated as hypotheses with confidence <= 0.35 pending a follow-up search. 2025-26 and 2026-27 win-loss totals deliberately left null rather than guessed. Age assumes a 1985 birth year (reported as 40 at hiring in June 2025).
